activity.role: Commander of US First Tank Brigade (later 304th Tank Brigade) in World War I
activity.notes: 1918 representative combat-service POINT for the American tank brigade that Patton led at the September St. Mihiel and Meuse-Argonne campaigns. US Army describes the formation as First Tank Brigade during St. Mihiel and later 304th Tank Brigade; do not apply its later unit designation retroactively as though it held that name at the start of September. This is NOT a complete 1918-to-1921 career rail nor proof he commanded for only one year. Other peacetime and intermediate staff/command billets belong in person biography, not separate ATLAS time-axis Activities.

sources.title: U.S. Army — The Birth of Armored Forces
sources.citation_text: US Army describes Patton leading First Tank Brigade in September 1918 at St. Mihiel and Meuse-Argonne, the historically prominent U.S. tank combat command.

sources.title: U.S. Army Center of Military History — St. Mihiel 12–16 September 1918
sources.citation_text: Army history identifies Patton's tank formation, later indexed as 304th, in the St. Mihiel operation of September 1918.
